title: Unit – 4 : Session – 12 : SLO – 1  |  Hashing — Introduction
sections: Hashing is used to perform efficient SEARCHING (insertion/deletion/lookup).
A HASH FUNCTION maps keys to indices.
A good hash function distributes keys UNIFORMLY (evenly).
When two keys hash to the same index, it's called a COLLISION.
Collision RESOLUTION (handling) techniques handle situations when two keys hash to same index.
OPEN ADDRESSING and CHAINING are two major collision resolution techniques.
In open addressing, all elements are stored in the same TABLE (array).
In chaining, each bucket contains a LINKED LIST.
LOAD FACTOR is the ratio of number of elements to table size.
A hash function should be EASY (fast) to compute.
LINEAR PROBING handles collision by checking the next slot.
Quadratic probing uses a QUADRATIC FUNCTION (i^2) to find next slot.
DOUBLE HASHING uses a second hash function to calculate step size.
Hash tables are widely used in DATABASES and COMPILERS (caching/dictionaries).
The time complexity of hashing for search in average case is O(1).
